channel.title: Dylan Gaeta: News
channel.description: Research, fieldwork, conferences, teaching, and milestones from Dylan Gaeta, Ph.D.

item.title: New paper in Communications Earth & Environment on U.S. oil and gas methane
item.description: New paper out in Communications Earth & Environment: U.S. oil and gas methane emission intensity declined 2019–2024 with little indication of federal policy impact.

item.title: Attended the CIRES Science Summit at CU Boulder
item.description: Attended the CIRES Science Summit at the University of Colorado Boulder, a full-day, in-person CIRES science meeting.

item.title: Launched snowdrought.org
item.description: We launched snowdrought.org, the Western US Climate and Snow Drought Explorer: an interactive dashboard of maps, time series, seasonal cycles, and cross-product anomalies of snow, water, carbon, and vegetation across the Western U.S. from 1990 to 2026.

item.title: Attended the OCO-2 v11 MIP modeling workshop at CU Boulder
item.description: Attended the OCO-2 v11 Model Intercomparison Project (MIP) modeling workshop at CU Boulder. The MIP is a collaboration among atmospheric CO₂ modelers studying the impact of assimilating OCO-2 retrievals in flux inversions.

item.title: Attended the 4th annual AIRDC workshop at George Mason University
item.description: Attended the 4th annual Greater Washington, D.C. Air Quality Research and Development Consortium (AIRDC) Workshop at George Mason University on June 9, held alongside the launch of George Mason's Center for Satellite and Earth Science Research.

item.title: Presented a poster at GMAC 2026 in Boulder
item.description: Presented a poster at GMAC 2026, the 53rd NOAA Global Monitoring Annual Conference in Boulder: A decline but no cessation of methyl bromide emissions from the United States over 2007–2018. The work uses tall tower, observatory, and aircraft flask measurements of CH₃Br from the NOAA GGGRN with a geostatistical inverse model to estimate U.S. emissions across the Montreal Protocol phase-out years (abstract volume).

item.title: Presented a poster at the 21st annual CIRES Rendezvous
item.description: Presented a poster at the 21st annual CIRES Rendezvous in Boulder: A decline in U.S. methyl bromide emissions throughout 2007–2021, in the Environmental Monitoring and Observations session.

item.title: Attended the Johns Hopkins Science Diplomacy Summit in Washington, D.C.
item.description: Attended the third annual Johns Hopkins Science Diplomacy Summit at the Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C., with sessions on AI, quantum, climate innovation, health, space, Arctic science, and research security.

item.title: Started as a postdoc at CIRES and NOAA GML
item.description: Started as a Postdoctoral Research Associate at CIRES (University of Colorado Boulder) and the NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, working on a NOAA/NIDIS-funded project on drought and carbon cycle dynamics in the Western U.S. The work combines NOAA GGGRN flask measurements, satellite data (FluxSat, TROPOMI, OCO-2, GRACE), ERA5-Land, and the SiB4 land surface model (CIRES profile).

item.title: Our sulfuryl fluoride research in a CCST report for California
item.description: The California Council on Science and Technology released its report on structural fumigation with sulfuryl fluoride for California's Department of Pesticide Regulation, drawing on our 2024 paper and including our U.S. emissions estimates.

item.title: Completed my Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins University
item.description: Officially completed my Ph.D. in Geography & Environmental Engineering at Johns Hopkins University.

item.title: New paper in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics on Arctic and boreal methane
item.description: New paper out in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics: Methane fluxes from Arctic & boreal North America: comparisons between process-based estimates and atmospheric observations, comparing process-based methane flux estimates with atmospheric observations across Arctic and boreal North America.

item.title: New paper in JGR Atmospheres on global wetland methane
item.description: New paper out in JGR Atmospheres: Spatial and temporal distribution of global wetland methane emissions during 2019–2020 estimated from satellite observations.

item.title: Defended my Ph.D. dissertation at Johns Hopkins University
item.description: Defended my dissertation at Johns Hopkins University: U.S. emissions of trace gas air pollutants inferred from a long-term atmospheric measurement network: from fumigants to fossil fuels. Three case studies use NOAA flask measurements and a geostatistical inverse model to map U.S. emissions: California dominates U.S. emissions of sulfuryl fluoride, mostly from structural fumigation for drywood termites. Methyl bromide emissions fell after the Montreal Protocol phase-out but not to zero, sustained by quarantine and pre-shipment uses and California strawberry growing. Oil and gas basins, led by the Permian, Anadarko, Eagle Ford, and Haynesville, dominate U.S. propane, butane, and pentane emissions, with implications for ozone downwind.

item.title: New paper in Atmospheric Measurement Techniques on the ChiWIS instrument
item.description: New paper out in Atmospheric Measurement Techniques describing the airborne Chicago Water Isotope Spectrometer: The airborne Chicago Water Isotope Spectrometer: An integrated cavity output spectrometer for measurements of the HDO/H₂O isotopic ratio in the Asian Summer Monsoon. I worked with the ChiWIS team during the 2017 StratoClim campaign in Nepal.

item.title: Attended the 3rd annual AIRDC workshop at Johns Hopkins University
item.description: Attended the 3rd annual Greater Washington, D.C. Air Quality Research and Development Consortium (AIRDC) Workshop, hosted by Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

item.title: Presented a poster at the JHU Sustainability Symposium
item.description: Presented a poster at the JHU Sustainability Symposium: Tracking U.S. pesticide emissions using atmospheric measurements and inverse modeling.

item.title: Joined Scale AI as a Human Frontier Collective Specialist
item.description: Joined Scale AI (remote) as a Human Frontier Collective Specialist (GenAI), developing evaluation frameworks and contributing climate science and atmospheric chemistry domain expertise to assess and improve next-generation generative AI models.

item.title: Co-led the Death Valley field course for the fourth year
item.description: Co-led Case Studies in Climate Change (Field Course) (EN.570.321) for the fourth year as Field Trip Co-leader: an annual 8-day field course for 10 undergraduate students in Death Valley National Park and the Eastern Sierras that focuses on past, present, and future climate change in California.

item.title: Passed my Graduate Board Oral exam at Johns Hopkins
item.description: Passed my Graduate Board Oral exam at Johns Hopkins, presenting my dissertation proposal: two chapters on U.S. fumigant emissions (sulfuryl fluoride and methyl bromide) and one on propane, butane, and pentane emissions from U.S. oil and gas regions and their air quality impacts.

item.title: Attended the NIST/NOAA urban greenhouse gas workshop in Washington, D.C.
item.description: Attended a half-day workshop at the Data Foundation in Washington, D.C., hosted by NIST and NOAA to shape a new consortium on city- and regional-scale greenhouse gas emissions information. The workshop brought together inventory developers, local and state governments, utilities, and researchers to discuss how atmospheric CO₂ and methane measurements and modeling can better serve the people who compile emissions inventories.

item.title: Gave a talk and presented a poster at AGU 2024 in Washington, D.C.
item.description: Gave an oral talk and presented a poster at the AGU Fall Meeting in Washington, D.C., covering two of my dissertation chapters: Emissions of C₃–C₅ alkanes from the U.S. fossil fuel industry and implications for air quality (talk, A42E-06) and U.S. emissions of methyl bromide have declined since the Montreal Protocol phase-out, but not to zero (poster, A21H-1855).

item.title: Attended the BSEC annual meeting in Baltimore
item.description: Attended the annual meeting of the Baltimore Social-Environmental Collaborative (BSEC) in Baltimore. BSEC is the DOE-funded Urban Integrated Field Lab led by Johns Hopkins, bringing together scientists from several universities and national labs with Baltimore communities to study urban climate, air, and water.

item.title: New paper in Environmental Science & Technology on U.S. ethane emissions
item.description: New paper out in Environmental Science & Technology: U.S. ethane emissions and trends estimated from atmospheric observations.

item.title: New paper in Remote Sensing of Environment on OCO-2 and the seasonal carbon cycle
item.description: New paper out in Remote Sensing of Environment: The Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 (OCO-2) and in situ CO₂ data suggest a larger seasonal amplitude of the terrestrial carbon cycle compared to many dynamic global vegetation models.

item.title: Received the Outstanding Doctoral TA Award
item.description: Received the Outstanding Doctoral TA Award from the Johns Hopkins Department of Environmental Health & Engineering.

item.title: Attended the 2nd annual AIRDC workshop at George Mason University
item.description: Attended the 2nd annual Greater Washington, D.C. Air Quality Research and Development Consortium (AIRDC) Workshop at George Mason University in Fairfax, VA.

item.title: My first first-author paper, in Communications Earth & Environment
item.description: My first first-author paper is out in Communications Earth & Environment: California dominates U.S. emissions of the pesticide and potent greenhouse gas sulfuryl fluoride. We find that California emits 60–85% of U.S. sulfuryl fluoride (0.26 ± 0.10 Gg/yr), equal to 5.5–12% of global emissions. The study was covered by The Guardian, the Los Angeles Times, Scientific American, The Hill, and others (media).

item.title: Gave a talk at AGU 2023 in San Francisco
item.description: Gave an oral talk at the AGU Fall Meeting in San Francisco: Trends in California's methyl bromide emissions from 2004–2022 estimated using atmospheric measurements and inverse modeling (A24I-08), in the session Scientific Impact of Long-Term Observations of the Atmosphere.

item.title: Taught a new seminar course at Johns Hopkins
item.description: Taught SOUL: Greenhouse Gases in Earth's Atmosphere (AS.360.111) at Johns Hopkins as SOUL Instructor. I wrote a proposal and was successfully funded to teach this new 1.0-credit seminar course for 10 students, which explored the mechanistic (process-based) relationship between GHGs and Earth's climate.

item.description: Passed my Doctoral Qualifying Exam in the Johns Hopkins Department of Environmental Health & Engineering.

item.title: New paper in Geophysical Research Letters on U.S. methane emissions trends
item.description: New paper out in Geophysical Research Letters: Inter-annual variability in atmospheric transport complicates estimation of US methane emissions trends.

item.description: Led analysis and report writing for Baltimore's official Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory for reporting years 2018–2020 with the Baltimore Office of Sustainability, including an assessment of COVID-19 related impacts on emissions and progress toward Baltimore's net-zero emissions target.
